messages:
Ana Torres: Quick sync — proposing a narrowed MVP for the Optimize toolkit. Focus: (1) automated batching recommendations, (2) cache suggestions (prefix/KV policy hints), (3) conservative quantization recommendations (no 4-bit auto-apply), and (4) eval-triggered alerts for regressions. Goal: useful product for customers like Acme Health and Chatly in 6–8 weeks. Thoughts?

Mike Chen: +1 to narrowed scope. Suggest we split into two phases: Phase A (batching + basic cache hints + alert hooks) and Phase B (quantization advisor + granular policy engine). Phase B needs model-level eval infra.

Cheng Li: From infra POV — Phase A is doable in 6 weeks if we accept limited integrations: console UI + webhook notifications. Batching recs can be heuristic: analyze request size distribution + token-per-request over 7 days. Cache hints require runtime flag `cacheable: true` at route-level or an inference hint API.

Sophia Patel: UX note — customers want a simple explainer for recommendations. Example card: "Increase batch_size to 32 for model X (expected 18% cost reduction, +10ms latency)". For alerts, surface failing evals with sample prompts and diffed outputs. I'll sketch cards if we lock fields.

Ana Torres: Good. Proposed acceptance criteria for Phase A (MVP):
- batching suggestions generated from last-7d traffic for a selected route
- cacheability hints surfaced with rationale (hit rate estimate)
- alerting when eval metric delta > configured threshold (default 3%)
- Console cards + webhook + email summary
- docs and one-runbook for SRE
Are these reasonable?

Mike Chen: Reasonable. A few clarifications:
- "batching suggestions" = recommended batch_size + expected throughput/cost delta; we should include an override button in Console and an API return for terraform ops.
- For alerts, we should support both absolute and relative thresholds.

Cheng Li: Dependencies / risks:
- Need a lightweight offline job to compute per-route distributions (kubernetes cronjob).
- Cache hit-rate estimator depends on being able to sample keys — privacy concerns for regulated customers (Acme Health). We'll provide a histogram-only mode (no PII) + opt-in sampling.
- Quantization recs (Phase B) require per-model eval harness + validation on quantized checkpoints. That’s a 3–4 week infra lift after Phase A.

Sophia Patel: For the Console card fields I need: model, route, current_batch, recommended_batch, estimated_cost_pct_change, latency_estimate_ms, confidence_score, rationale (1–2 lines).

Ana Torres: Noted. Also, customers asked for an "Experiment" toggle so they can A/B test recommended batch sizes without changing production config. Doable?

Mike Chen: Implementable with traffic-split routing via existing rollout layer. Minor work to wire metrics. Adds complexity but high value.

Cheng Li: Ops question: how do we prevent bad recommendations from causing SLO regressions? We should gate recommendations behind a canary flow: 1) dry-run simulation, 2) small traffic experiment (5–10%), 3) escalate. Add automatic rollback if latency breaches + error rate increases.

Ana Torres: Agreed — add automatic rollback to acceptance criteria for Phase A experiments.

Sophia Patel: On alerts UI: provide two actions on an alert card: "Open eval diff" and "Create experiment". Also a short JSON payload for webhooks. Sample webhook:\n```json\n{\n  "route": "/chat/generate",\n  "model": "redwood-qa-v2",\n  "metric": "exact_match",\n  "baseline": 0.912,\n  "current": 0.873,\n  "delta_pct": -4.3,\n  "recommended_action": "run-eval"\n}\n```

Mike Chen: That webhook shape is fine. For batching recs we'll return this example payload from API:\n```json\n{\n  "model": "redwood-llama-13b",\n  "route": "/summarize",\n  "current_batch": 8,\n  "recommended_batch": 24,\n  "expected_cost_reduction_pct": 18.2,\n  "expected_p90_latency_ms_delta": 12,\n  "confidence": "medium"\n}\n```

Cheng Li: Timeline proposal:
- Week 0–1: instrumentation + data pipeline for request distributions
- Week 2–3: batching recommendation engine + API return
- Week 4: console card UX + experiment wiring
- Week 5: alerting hookup + webhook payloads + docs
- Week 6: internal dogfood + roll to early access customers
Estimate +/− 1 week.

Ana Torres: Team votes: are we committing to Phase A (6 weeks, EA customers only)? Reply with :thumbsup: for yes.

Mike Chen: :thumbsup:
Cheng Li: :thumbsup: (with the histogram-only sample mode for privacy)
Sophia Patel: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-notice: staging job for data pipeline scheduled for 30m from now.

Ana Torres: Great — I'll draft a short PRD with launch criteria, dependencies, and action owners. Action list now: Ana = PRD + customer comms, Mike = API + experiment wiring, Cheng = infra + privacy mode, Sophia = Console mocks, docs = rotation. Target EA launch date: 6 weeks from today.

Mike Chen: I'll start a tracking ticket and link infra/tasks.

Cheng Li: I'll provision a cronjob and a data retention policy for sampled histograms.

Sophia Patel: I'll post mockups by EOD Thursday.

Ana Torres: Thanks team — will follow up with PRD and invite Acme Health for EA feedback. :rocket:
